agency.name: New Hampshire Department of Revenue Administration

social_security.summary: New Hampshire has no tax on wages, pensions or benefits, and its Interest and Dividends Tax is repealed for 2025, so Social Security is not taxed by the state.

sources.quote: For tax periods beginning on or after January 1, 2025, New Hampshire taxpayers are no longer required to pay the state’s Interest and Dividends Tax.

public_pension.summary: New Hampshire has no broad personal income tax, so government pensions are not taxed by the state.

sources.quote: For tax periods beginning on or after January 1, 2025, New Hampshire taxpayers are no longer required to pay the state’s Interest and Dividends Tax.

private_pension.summary: New Hampshire has no broad personal income tax, so private pensions, 401(k) and IRA distributions are not taxed by the state.

sources.quote: For tax periods beginning on or after January 1, 2025, New Hampshire taxpayers are no longer required to pay the state’s Interest and Dividends Tax.

military_retirement.summary: New Hampshire has no broad personal income tax, so military retired pay is not taxed by the state.

sources.quote: For tax periods beginning on or after January 1, 2025, New Hampshire taxpayers are no longer required to pay the state’s Interest and Dividends Tax.

notes: New Hampshire never taxed wages, pensions or Social Security; its only personal income tax was the Interest and Dividends Tax (RSA 77), which was repealed for tax periods beginning on or after January 1, 2025 (HB 2 of 2023). Returns for 2024 and earlier remain due. The Department page is read from an Internet Archive capture because www.revenue.nh.gov's robots.txt refuses automated readers. No statute source is given: the quoted page states the repeal directly.
